subject: Cost model rebucket & implementation credit — Clearpath evaluation

messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma.liu@clearpath.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Cole <jared.cole@runtimeai.com>
Date: 2026-07-31T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up — cost buckets and onboarding credits

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week. We liked Redwood's latency profile but need to reconcile a few things before we can recommend a change to our procurement committee. Two quick asks: 1) Can you show a sample rebucketing of our monthly runtime fees if we move from a blended seat + reserved GPU model to a pure consumption model with token tiers? 2) We typically ask for implementation/onboarding credits to cover integration work — what level of credit would you offer for a 12‑month committed relationship?

To help, I attached our last two months of invoices and a simple traffic heatmap (see attachments). We're targeting a decision by mid‑August.

—Emma
Head of Cloud Ops, Clearpath Logistics

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@clearpath.com>
Date: 2026-07-31T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up — cost buckets and onboarding credits

Hi Emma — great to hear and thanks for the files.

Short answer: yes. I put together a high‑level rebucket proposal and an implementation credit outline for a 12‑month committed plan (see attached PDF + SOW stub). The proposal assumes:
- Baseline token unit price with volume tiers at 0–5M / 5–20M / 20M+ per month
- An onboarding credit equal to 20% of estimated first‑quarter consumption to cover integration and runbook work (can be structured as service credit or one‑time invoice credit)
- A limited SLA uplift clause for the first 3 months if you commit to a 12‑month term

If that looks directionally right I can schedule a short call to walk through the numbers and surface any technical constraints (KV cache warm‑up, egress assumptions, burst rates). We kept the proposal conservative on savings so you can see upside if traffic skews to lower token sizes.

Proposed next step: 30‑minute cost walk‑through tomorrow or Thursday. When works best?

Thanks,
Olga
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood_rebucket_proposal_v1.pdf)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-31T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pricing follow-up — cost buckets and onboarding credits

Jonas / Rachel — forwarding Emma's ask plus the quick proposal I drafted. TL;DR: Clearpath wants a cleaner consumption model and ~20% onboarding credit. Key negotiation points I want your input on before the customer call:

Jonas — technical: can we commit to the burst behaviour assumed in page 4 of the PDF? The customer has a few 30–90s traffic spikes tied to batch jobs. I want to be explicit about KV cache effects and any warm‑up delta we should bake into the proposal.

Rachel — commercial: 20% of Q1 consumption as a credit is our ask — do we have margin runway for that at a 12‑month commit and a 10% net discount across token tiers? Also any guidance on structuring the credit (invoice credit vs service credit) to avoid revenue recognition headaches.

I'm planning to offer a conditional clause: full onboarding credit at commit OR scaled credit if they choose a 6‑month term. Thoughts?

—Olga
(Onward: attachments referenced)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Liu <emma.liu@clearpath.com>, Jared Cole <jared.cole@runtimeai.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-07-31T15:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing follow-up — cost buckets and onboarding credits

Emma / Jared — thanks for the quick turn. Based on your invoices and the traffic heatmap I ran a conservative rebucket scenario and a paired commercial structure that keeps Clearpath's first‑quarter cash exposure predictable. Highlights: 

1) Pricing buckets (monthly token consumption):
   • 0–5M tokens: $0.0024 / token
   • 5M–20M tokens: $0.0018 / token
   • 20M+ tokens: $0.00145 / token
   These numbers include a 10% term discount if you sign a 12‑month commitment.

2) Onboarding credit: 20% of estimated first‑quarter consumption applied as either:
   • Invoice credit (preferred by Clearpath for accounting simplicity) OR
   • Service credit (applied to professional services SOW) — we can accommodate either, but invoice credit requires a signed addendum at contract start.

3) SLA carveout during onboarding: for months 0–3 we include a 15‑minute remediation target for high‑impact incidents and a 50% credit cap for uptime SLA misses related specifically to KV cache warm‑ups or customer integration issues. Full SLA reverts after month 3.

4) Implementation SOW: attached stub lists standard tasks — ingress mapping, KV cache tuning, integration runbook, 2x on‑site/remote knowledge transfer sessions. Estimated 4–6 engineer days. If you prefer, we can convert some of the credit to additional onboarding days.

Next steps: I'm available for a 30‑minute review Thursday 9–11am PT or Friday 1–3pm PT. If that works, I'll send a calendar invite and a one‑page comparison that shows your current blended seat+reserved spend vs the proposed consumption model at your observed traffic distribution.

If you want a quicker price anchor now: with the proposed buckets and the 20% onboarding invoice credit, Clearpath's modeled month‑one cash outflow is ~22% lower than your current blended bill (conservative projection).

Attachments: redwood_rebucket_proposal_v1.pdf, sow_implementation_stub.docx

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
